editorial.meta_description: The ACCA Advanced Performance Management exam is scheduled for retirement on 2027-06-30. The official successor for this professional certification is SPI.
editorial.overview: Advanced Performance Management is a professional-level certification provided by the ACCA. It focuses on the application of strategic planning and control models to monitor organizational performance. The exam evaluates how candidates analyze external influences, measure performance, and apply management information systems. It serves as a final professional assessment, requiring candidates to demonstrate high-level analytical skills in complex business environments before the exam is retired in favor of SPI. This assessment ensures that students are prepared for the demands of modern financial leadership roles.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for professional accounting students aiming to demonstrate advanced expertise in performance management. Candidates should possess a strong grasp of financial reporting and management accounting principles to navigate the complex, linear-format assessments required by the ACCA at this professional level.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Candidates should review technical articles and past exam papers to understand the requirement format. Practice applying models to scenarios. Focus on integrating knowledge from previous levels, as the exam requires synthesis of skills. Ensure familiarity with the 195-minute time limit and the mix of objective test questions and constructed response tasks to manage the exam pace effectively. Consistent practice with past papers is a standard method for achieving the required 50 score.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the use of strategic planning and control models to monitor organizational performance. It requires candidates to apply theoretical frameworks to real-world business scenarios to ensure organizational objectives are met through effective planning and monitoring processes.

This domain examines how external factors impact organizational performance. Candidates must identify and evaluate how various external influences affect business strategy and performance measurement, requiring an understanding of the broader economic and competitive environment in which organizations operate today.

This domain focuses on the development and application of performance measurement systems. It involves selecting appropriate metrics and indicators to evaluate organizational success, ensuring that performance data aligns with strategic goals and provides actionable insights for management teams.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a 195-minute linear assessment. Candidates must manage their time across objective test questions and constructed response sections. Ensure you read all requirements carefully, as the format demands precise application of knowledge to the provided scenarios to succeed.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam consists of a mix of Objective Test Questions and Constructed Response questions. While the specific number of questions is not fixed, candidates must be prepared to address both formats within the 195-minute duration to demonstrate their full competency in the subject matter.

To successfully pass the Advanced Performance Management exam, candidates are required to achieve a minimum score of 50. This threshold reflects the professional standard expected of students at this level of the ACCA qualification and ensures mastery of the core performance management concepts.

The total duration for the exam is 195 minutes. Candidates should plan their time carefully to ensure they have sufficient opportunity to address all sections of the assessment, including the objective test questions and the more complex constructed response tasks provided during the session.

faq.question_title: What is the replacement for this exam?
faq.answer_text: The ACCA has officially scheduled the retirement of this exam for 2027-06-30. Following this date, the official successor exam will be SPI. Students are encouraged to plan their studies accordingly to ensure a smooth transition to the new qualification path provided by the ACCA.

methodology.summary: This editorial was developed by synthesizing official ACCA exam documentation, technical articles, and verified exam metadata to provide a clear, accurate overview of the APM certification and its transition to the SPI successor exam for all current students.
